status: frozen 2026-11-04 after reading one published test log (GPT-5 pillow 290, features 1 and 4) and CooperBench's pass check, before re-scoring any other log
question: CooperBench's evaluation code counts a test run as failed when its output contains 'failed' anywhere, in any case, including warnings and install logs. Does that explain the paper's recorded merged failures that our re-test does not reproduce, and how does a correct pass check change the paper's coop results and our census labels?
from_note: dataset revision, models, excluded repos, the census's failed pairs, own-patch tests and merged re-tests all come from the paper census and the upstream check
logs: for every usable GPT-5 and Claude coop pair, the merge report published next to its patches ({model}_{repo}_task{id}_merge_report_f{a}_into_f{b}_k1.json): each feature's naive, union and llm test output, where present
paper_check: re-implemented from CooperBench's evaluation/test_runner.py (commit 95cd5a2): tests ran if the output matches (passed|PASSED|Test execution completed|\bok\b); a run passes if tests ran, the output matches (\bok\b|passed|PASSED), and it does not match (FAIL:|FAILED|failed.*tests?.*failed) ignoring case

corrected_check.pytest: used when the log has a pytest summary line ('=== ... in N.NNs ===' after removing ANSI codes): every such line reports at least one passed and no failed or error; 'no tests ran' fails
corrected_check.go: else, when the log has go test package lines: at least one 'ok' line, and no 'FAIL' or '--- FAIL' line, 'panic:' or '[build failed]'
corrected_check.cargo: else, when the log has 'test result:' lines: all of them 'ok'
corrected_check.jest_vitest: else, when the log has a 'Tests:' summary: at least one passed and none failed, and no failed test suite
corrected_check.unparsed: otherwise the recorded result is kept, and the case is counted

measurements.check: agreement of the re-implemented paper check with the recorded result over all logs
measurements.flips: per model and stage, recorded results the corrected check reverses, in both directions, with the line that triggered the paper check
measurements.coop: coop success on the paper's pipeline (a pair passes if any stage passes both features), recorded and corrected
measurements.retest: on clean pairs whose merge is clean in our harness too, agreement of the recorded and the corrected naive result with our merged re-test
measurements.census: the paper census re-labeled with corrected merged results; own-patch tests and solo references unchanged; pairs the correction makes pass leave the census and are counted

decision_rule: Primary: among the census's unreproduced merged failures (clean pairs where the paper's naive merge failed the feature, our merge is also clean and our re-test passes it), the share the corrected check scores as passed. If it is at least half, the paper's pass check explains most of the non-reproduction: the census is re-labeled with corrected merged results and the gap-pair integration share is reported again under the census's rule. If it is below half, the cause lies elsewhere (flaky tests or environment) and the next step re-runs those tests in Docker. Check: the re-implemented paper check must match the recorded result on at least 95% of logs, or the analysis stops, because then we are not scoring what the paper scored. The published solo runs have no test logs, so solo results cannot be corrected here; any coop-solo comparison after correction is one-sided and reported as such.
results: rescore_rows.csv and rescore_summary.json in the output directory
